problems.statement:
With the help of a school telescope examine and draw the details visible on the Sun's disk. Mark the cardinal points on your drawing.

[[figure:p1-fig1]]

Identify the details of your drawing with the details of the one-dimensional radio profiles of the Sun obtained in the previous days by RATAN-600. Mark them by the corresponding letters.

The radio observations were carried out at noon, the knife beam was directed vertically and covered all the Sun's disk.

[[figure:p1-fig2]]

solution.statement:
Example supplied in the archive, dated 23 October 1998:

[[figure:p1-sol-fig1]]

The supplied radio profiles are annotated with the corresponding A, B, C and D features and their projected motion:

problems.statement:
> ...That telescope was christened the Star-Splitter,  
> Because it didn't do a thing but split  
> A star in two or three, the way you split  
> A globule of quicksilver in your hand  
> With one stroke of your finger in the middle...  

Robert Frost, “The Star-Splitter”

Using a school telescope find in the sky and resolve several ($\leq5$) binary stars into their components.

Notice the brightnesses and the colours of the components.

Explain the relationship between the brightnesses and the colours of the components.

solution.statement:
The archive supplies one illustrative observation: an orange main component and a white companion. It gives $M_{\mathrm{main\ comp.}}>M_{\mathrm{comp.}}$ and states: “Main comp is in the red giant evolution phase. The companion is remaining in the main sequence.” The accompanying luminosity–spectral-type diagram is retained below.

[[figure:p2-sol-fig1]]

figures.alt: Original example row showing component colours, evolutionary explanation and luminosity–spectral-type sketch; the first character of the object designation is partly illegible.

solution.incompleteReason: The first character of the handwritten example star designation is partly illegible in the source; the source crop is retained without guessing that character. The example explanation and diagram are otherwise present.
